messages:
maya: Heads up — CI dashboard just alerted a sustained drop in rerank NDCG after we merged the quantize branch for the new embedder. Looks like it's consistent across a few runs, not just a flake. Screenshot: https://redwood.internal/s/qsx
sam: Ugh. Which runner config did the CI use? quantize jobs sometimes run a different aggregator/metric impl.
priya: CI used the new runner image (runner:quantize-v2). I ran a local eval and saw variance too but smaller. Suspect a tie-breaking / topk sorting nondeterminism.
oliver: Can you paste the runner config? also check if shard keys changed — we've had fold-merge issues before.
maya: config snippet:
```
runner:
  seed: 12345
  deterministic: false
  shard_by_query: true
  topk: 100
model:
  quantized: true
  backend: cuda
```
priya: deterministic:false is a red flag for CI evals. The old baseline runs with deterministic:true. Also our aggregator sorts by score only — ties get arbitrary order across runs.
sam: That would explain small but systematic NDCG shifts when quantized reduces score precision. Quick fix: enforce stable tie-breaker: score then doc_id.
oliver: Suggest replacing sorting with stable key tuple:
```python
# old
topk = sorted(candidates, key=lambda x: x.score, reverse=True)
# new
topk = sorted(candidates, key=lambda x: (x.score, x.doc_id), reverse=True)
```
priya: Also set deterministic:true and pin seed in CI: runner.seed -> 42 across runs. I'll open a tiny PR for both changes.
ci-bot: build 5872 (runner-quantize-v2) failed metric-check: rerank-ndcg drop > 1.5% vs baseline. See: https://ci.redwood/build/5872
dana: Another possibility: dashboard aggregation buckets quantized runs into a different date partition — we saw earlier that one partition had truncated fold counts. If you merge folds with unequal counts, NDCG averages can skew. I'll check the analytics join.
maya: Thanks. Action items I hear:
- priya: PR to make runner deterministic + stable tie-breaker (seed pinned)
- dana: check dashboard fold aggregation and partition bug
- sam/oliver: run a controlled single-fold eval (no sharding) comparing float vs quantized with same seed and sort logic
I'll attach a minimal repro command I used locally:
```
python -m eval_runner.run \
  --model models/new-embedder:latest \
  --quantize --quant-level q4_0 \
  --queries datasets/mteb-like/queries.jsonl \
  --deterministic --seed 42 --topk 100
```
sam: I'll run that and post results here.
oliver: If the repro still shows >1% drop after deterministic+stable-sort, next step is to diff scoring at item level to see whether quantization changes relative ranking or just score scaling.
priya: PR opened: https://git.redwood/p/runner/+/2345 — includes stable-sort, deterministic true in default CI profile, and a small unit test asserting identical reorder for same seed.
maya: Great. Let's wait for CI with those changes; if dashboard still reports drift, we'll dig deeper into fold merging and per-item score diffs. :eyes:
ci-bot: triggered run 5873 with runner-quantize-v2 + stable-sort patch. Status: queued.
sam: ran the local repro, attaching brief diff: float vs quantized topk reorder count = 6/100, ndcg delta = -0.9% (so lower but under 1%). I'll upload full CSV to the artifact bucket.
priya: Good sign — stable-sort reduced noise. dana any findings on partitioning?
dana: found a bug in the analytics ETL: when a run has shard_by_query:true we were summing fold sizes from an outdated index which led to fold_count mismatch for ~12 runs. Patching ETL now.
maya: Perfect. Closing loop once CI 5873 and ETL patch land. If either still shows systematic gap we'll escalate to quantization team for eval-aware calibration. Thanks all.
